input.file_text: # Metropolitan Museum of Art Inventory - Standardized TSV ## Overview This directory contains a standardized version of the Metropolitan Museum of Art inventory TSV file with complete data integrity preservation through SHA256 checksums. **Status:** ✓ Standardized with fixity verification **Records:** 441 art objects **Last Updated:** 2025 --- ## Files in This Package ### Primary Data File - **`met_inventory_standardized.tsv`** — The standardized inventory file - 4 columns: Date, Title, Object_Number, Museum_Link - 441 data rows + 1 header row = 442 total lines - UTF-8 encoding, tab-delimited, LF line endings - 100% data preservation from original ### Documentation - **`STANDARDIZATION_REPORT.md`** — Detailed report of all changes made - Issues identified in original file - Standardization rules applied - Special cases handled - Complete before/after comparisons - **`VERIFY_INTEGRITY.md`** — How to verify file integrity - Platform-specific checksum verification instructions - Troubleshooting guide - Long-term preservation recommendations - Example workflows - **`SHA256_CHECKSUMS.txt`** — Checksum values for integrity verification - SHA256 hash of standardized TSV file - File size and line count - Verification commands ### Code Tools - **`fixity_verification.py`** — Python script to verify and document checksums - Calculates SHA256 hash - Generates verification reports - Can be run anytime to validate file integrity --- ## Quick Start ### 1. Understanding the Data The standardized file contains: | Column | Content | Completeness | |--------|---------|-------------| | **Date** | Object creation period or dating range | 435 dated; 6 marked [Unknown] | | **Title** | Object name, title, or description | 426 titled; 15 marked [Untitled] | | **Object_Number** | Museum accession/catalog number | 441/441 (100%) | | **Museum_Link** | Direct URL to Met Museum online collection | 441/441 (100%) | **Example rows:** ``` Date Title Object_Number Museum_Link 19th century [Untitled] 93.1.168 http://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/47519 ca. 1425 Bahman Taking Revenge on the Sistanians... 57.51.8 http://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/451391 1792 Chinese Chairs, in Chippendale Drawings, ... 20.40.1(23) http://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/390499 ``` ### 2. Verify File Integrity **Linux/macOS:** ```bash sha256sum -c SHA256_CHECKSUMS.txt ``` **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell certUtil -hashfile met_inventory_standardized.tsv SHA256 ``` ### 3. Use the File **Open in spreadsheet application:** - Excel: File → Open, select the TSV file, ensure UTF-8 encoding - Google Sheets: File → Import → Upload → Select this TSV - LibreOffice: File → Open, select the TSV file **Parse in code:** ```python import pandas as pd df = pd.read_csv('met_inventory_standardized.tsv', delimiter='\t') print(df.head()) ``` ```bash # Shell scripting while IFS=$'\t' read -r date title obj_num link; do echo "$date | $title | $obj_num" done < met_inventory_standardized.tsv | head -5 ``` --- ## What Changed from Original ### New Format - ✓ Clearer column names - ✓ No empty fields (replaced with [Untitled] or [Unknown]) - ✓ HTML entities decoded - ✓ Consistent UTF-8 encoding - ✓ Standard line endings (LF) ### Data Preserved - ✓ All 441 records intact - ✓ All URLs valid and complete - ✓ All object numbers unchanged - ✓ All dating information preserved - ✓ All titles and descriptions preserved - ✓ Multilingual content (Chinese, Japanese) preserved ### Examples of Changes **Empty titles populated:** ``` Before: 7th–9th century [TAB] [EMPTY] [TAB] 2002.556.36 After: 7th–9th century [TAB] [Untitled] [TAB] 2002.556.36 ``` **HTML entities decoded:** ``` Before: Arrowhead (<i>Yanone</i>) After: Arrowhead (Yanone) ``` **Column headers clarified:** ``` Before: Object Date | Title | Object Number | Link Resource After: Date | Title | Object_Number | Museum_Link ``` See **STANDARDIZATION_REPORT.md** for complete details. --- ## Data Quality Notes ### Completeness - 441/441 records have object numbers (100%) - 441/441 records have museum links (100%) - 426/441 records have titles (96.5%) - 435/441 records have dates (98.6%) ### Known Special Cases - Some object numbers include letter suffixes (a–c, .112) indicating related pieces - Some dates are ranges (18th–19th century) rather than specific years - 15 objects have no title listed (marked [Untitled]) - 6 objects have uncertain dates (marked [Unknown]) - 8 records include East Asian titles in Chinese and Japanese characters ### Data Limitations - This standardized version reflects the Met Museum's data as provided - For authoritative object information, consult the Museum's website directly - Some objects may have incomplete cataloging information --- ## Checksums for Integrity Verification **Algorithm:** SHA256 **Purpose:** Ensure file hasn't been corrupted or modified **How to use:** See **VERIFY_INTEGRITY.md** for detailed instructions **Checksum Details:** - Files included: met_inventory_standardized.tsv - Last verified: 2025 - Recalculate anytime using provided Python script --- ## Column Specifications ### Date Column - **Type:** String (date, date range, or marker) - **Nullable:** No ([Unknown] used instead) - **Examples:** - Specific year: "1793" - Estimated year: "ca. 1800" - Range: "18th–19th century" - Complex: "ca. 1981–1640 B.C." - Uncertain: "[Unknown]" ### Title Column - **Type:** String (object name or description) - **Nullable:** No ([Untitled] used instead) - **Max Length:** ~400 characters - **Examples:** - "Amulet of Ptah-Sokar" - "Andersonville Prison, Georgia, South-west View..." - "Design for a Four-Wheel Chaise" - "[Untitled]" ### Object_Number Column - **Type:** String (not numeric — contains letters and special characters) - **Nullable:** No - **Unique:** Yes (Museum's unique identifier) - **Format Examples:** - Simple: "2002.556.36" - With letters: "36.25.2605" - Multi-part: "2002.201.111, .112" - With codes: "Burdick 218, N224.6" ### Museum_Link Column - **Type:** URL (String) - **Format:** `http://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/[SEARCH_ID]` - **Nullable:** No - **Completeness:** 441/441 (100%) - **All links valid:** Yes (verified) --- ## Usage Examples ### Python with Pandas ```python import pandas as pd # Load the file df = pd.read_csv('met_inventory_standardized.tsv', sep='\t') # Get basic stats print(f"Total records: {len(df)}") print(f"Columns: {list(df.columns)}") # Find objects by date ceramic_19c = df[df['Date'] == '19th century'] print(f"19th century objects: {len(ceramic_19c)}") # Find untitled objects untitled = df[df['Title'] == '[Untitled]'] print(f"Untitled objects: {len(untitled)}") # Access a specific record first = df.iloc[0] print(f"First object: {first['Title']} ({first['Date']})") print(f"Link: {first['Museum_Link']}") ``` ### SQL (Import to Database) ```sql -- Import into SQLite .mode tabs .import met_inventory_standardized.tsv inventory -- Query examples SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory; SELECT * FROM inventory WHERE Date LIKE '%19th century%'; SELECT Title FROM inventory WHERE Title = '[Untitled]'; ``` ### Shell Script ```bash # Count records wc -l met_inventory_standardized.tsv # Extract all museum links cut -f4 met_inventory_standardized.tsv | tail -n +2 # Find objects from specific century grep "19th century" met_inventory_standardized.tsv | wc -l # Get random object shuf -n 1 met_inventory_standardized.tsv ``` --- ## Troubleshooting ### "File won't open in Excel" - Open Excel first, then File → Open - Select "Text Files" as file type - Choose UTF-8 encoding in import dialog - Select Tab as delimiter ### "Special characters display incorrectly" - Ensure your editor uses UTF-8 encoding (not ANSI, Windows-1252, etc.) - Try a different editor (VS Code, Sublime, Notepad++) - Verify file wasn't converted to a different encoding ### "Checksum doesn't match" - See **VERIFY_INTEGRITY.md** for troubleshooting - File may have been modified or corrupted in transit - Re-download the original file ### "Links to Met Museum are broken" - This data was standardized in 2025 - Museum may have updated their URLs since then - Try searching the object number on metmuseum.org directly --- ## Citation When using this standardized data, consider referencing: > Metropolitan Museum of Art Inventory (Standardized TSV, 2025). 441 records. Standardized with SHA256 fixity verification. [Your citation should also include the date accessed and any specific Met Museum credits] --- ## License & Attribution **Original Data Source:** The Metropolitan Museum of Art Collection Database https://www.metmuseum.org/ **Standardization:** Performed with preservation of all original data **Format:** Tab-Separated Values (TSV) **License:** Refer to Met Museum's usage terms This standardized version maintains all original data and adds structural improvements for better usability in analytical and archival contexts. --- ## Support & Questions ### For Issues with This Standardized File - Check **STANDARDIZATION_REPORT.md** for what changed - Review **VERIFY_INTEGRITY.md** for verification issues - Run the Python script to generate detailed verification reports ### For Questions About the Original Data - Visit https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection - Contact The Met's Collections Information Department - Review their data documentation --- ## Version History | Version | Date | Changes | |---------|------|---------| | 1.0 | 2025 | Initial standardization with SHA256 fixity verification | --- **Files included in this package:** 1. ✓ met_inventory_standardized.tsv (main data file) 2. ✓ SHA256_CHECKSUMS.txt (integrity verification) 3. ✓ STANDARDIZATION_REPORT.md (detailed change log) 4. ✓ VERIFY_INTEGRITY.md (verification instructions) 5. ✓ fixity_verification.py (Python verification script) 6. ✓ README.md (this file) --- *Questions about data standardization? See STANDARDIZATION_REPORT.md* *Issues with verification? See VERIFY_INTEGRITY.md* *Ready to analyze the data? Start with the TSV file above*
